unit.name: Reward models and RLHF over text generation
unit.description: Explains how pairwise preference data trains a reward model and how RLHF maps text generation into an RL problem with sparse terminal reward.
unit.summary: A reward model is introduced as a separate model trained to predict which responses humans prefer, moving alignment from imitating responses to modeling preferences [ts=5822s] [ts=5831s]. Labelers compare two or more SFT-generated responses to the same prompt, and the resulting preference data trains a scalar reward head initialized from the SFT model [ts=5853s] [ts=5914s] [ts=5922s]. The loss encourages higher predicted rewards for preferred answers, making the reward model a scalable proxy critic for human preferences during RLHF [ts=5995s] [ts=6013s] [ts=6058s]. In RLHF, the language model is the agent/policy, the state is the prompt plus generated tokens, the action is the next token, the reward comes from the reward model, and an episode is a full generated answer whose reward is usually observed only at the end [ts=6074s] [ts=6114s] [ts=6143s] [ts=6202s].

key_points.text: The reward model is a separate model trained to predict which responses humans prefer.
Reward-model data comes from labelers comparing multiple SFT-generated responses to the same prompt.
The reward model is initialized from the SFT model but replaces the language-model softmax output with a scalar reward head.
The reward-model loss encourages higher predicted reward for the human-preferred response than for the less preferred response.
After training, the reward model replaces humans as the evaluator during RLHF.
In RLHF, the language model is the agent, the state is prompt plus generated tokens so far, the action is the next token, and the reward is estimated by the reward model.
RLHF over text generation is a sparse-reward episodic task because the reward is typically observed after the full completion rather than at every token.

kp_catalog.name: RLHF preference optimization
kp_catalog.description: The RLHF reward-maximization objective with KL regularization and Bradley-Terry-style pairwise rewards. Optimizing language models for learned human preference rewards over model-generated outputs.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Important because rLHF preference optimization formalizes how the RLHF reward-maximization objective with KL regularization and Bradley-Terry-style pairwise rewards, which later units use as core machinery rather than background context.

kp_catalog.name: Reinforcement learning and RLHF for NLG
kp_catalog.description: Training text generators with reward functions, including human-preference reward models layered on top of pretrained systems.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Important because reinforcement learning and RLHF for NLG synthesizes training text generators with reward functions, including human-preference reward models layered on top of pretrained systems into an end-to-end method or integrated recipe.

kp_catalog.name: Language-model pretraining alignment gap
kp_catalog.description: Next-token prediction creates capable text continuation models but not necessarily models that answer helpfully, politely, or safely.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The LM helpfulness gap motivates RLHF, but it is not itself an RL prerequisite.
